record_title: Quantitative Bézout stability forces Banach–Mazur proximity to a simplex
limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The stability exponent 1/n and displayed constants are not claimed sharp. The Banach–Mazur coefficient n^(50n^2) is inherited from Böröczky’s Rogers–Shephard stability theorem. The relative-inradius modulus uses the full two-body Bézout constant, whereas the Banach–Mazur conclusion uses only the restricted chord-intersection tests. No reverse near-simplex-to-near-Bézout estimate or classification of near-extremizers is claimed. The motivating characterization is recent, so differently formulated or not-yet-indexed related work remains a residual originality risk.
